newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest BUX rebounds and hits new high.
newsitem.headline: Budapest BUX rebounds and hits new high.

text.p: The Budapest Stock Exchange followed its own path upwards on Friday rather than joining Europe's falling trend, traders said.
The BUX index more than regained Thursday's fall, finishing the week at a new record high of 5,438.35 points, up 68.20, propelled primarily by heavily traded shares of oil and gas company MOL.
"Certain stocks were under quite strong selling pressure by foreigners while on the other hand MOL surged, pushing the index higher," said Laszlo Baranyai of Gog Securities.
In heavy trade MOL shares exceeded the 3,000 forint psychological barrier following news of a 17 percent wage settlement for 1997.
"Fears of a possible strike were dispelled by this news," one trader said earlier today.
MOL shares opened at 2,800 forints, below Thursday's close of 2,850 forints, but then rapidly advanced to record territory. It finished eight percent higher at 3,080 forints.
Gainers included chemicals stocks Borsodchem and TVK. Both rebounded from Thursday's losses and closed at 6,150 forints, up 250 and at 2,600, up 35, respectively.

Elsewhere on the market the pharmaceuticals closed mixed with Richter and Egis falling to 11,150 forints, down 150 and to 11,635, down 135, respectively. But Human moved up 30 forints to close at 3,380.
Banks closed mixed, as OTP fell to 3,700, down 170 and Inter-Europa Bank rose 2,000 forints to 58,000.
Traders believe the market has to go through some correction after this year's gains of around 30 percent but they are convinced any new downturn it will be limited.
"After substantial rises a natural correction could come but no major fall should be expected," Baranyai said. "We might move a little lower next week."
With little fresh news on the macroeconomic side, preliminary annual corporate results, to be published by February 15, could give clues to further investments, traders said.
